newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers agree to re-open Athens bourse.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers agree to re-open Athens bourse.

text.p: Greek brokers said they accepted government proposals to defuse a crisis that has kept the Athens bourse closed for three days.
The exchange will open gradually, starting Wednesday.
Brokers association president Panayotis Kondalexis told reporters after an association meeting that the decision to resume trading was unanimous.
"We believe the conditions for resuming operations at the Athens stock exchange are satisfied," he said.

Kondalexis said the association asked for a fast clearing of all accounts on Wednesday and for a 15-30 minute delay in opening to facilitate the process. The delay could be made up after the regular closing time, he said.
"It is estimated that by tomorrow the majority of companies will have settled accounts," he said. "By Thursday we believe all will be cleared."
He said only companies with cleared accounts would trade on the bourse on Wednesday.
"The decision was unanimously made by all brokerage firms," he said.
